sentences.text: Based on extrapolation from related species, Gongbusaurus was a small, bipedal herbivore about 1.3 to 1.5 meters long.
The specific name shiyii is a pun meaning both "junior consultant" and "register of lost objects," referencing how the type teeth were found separately among other collected bones.
The genus Gongbusaurus was named and described by Dong, Zhou, and Zhang in 1983.
The genus was originally established based on two small teeth found in the holotype specimen IVPP V9069.
Fossils of the type species were found in the Oxfordian-age Upper Shaximiao Formation in Sichuan, China.
A second species, G. wucaiwanensis, was added in 1989 based on a fragmentary skeleton including a partial lower jaw and tail vertebrae.
The animal is thought to have been a strong runner.
Recent reviews classify Gongbusaurus as a dubious ornithischian and recommend renaming the better-known second species.
Gongbusaurus lived between approximately 160 and 157 million years ago during the Late Jurassic period.
The fossil record for Gongbusaurus spans from the Bathonian to the Oxfordian stages, between 168.2 and 154.8 million years ago.
It is debated whether Gongbusaurus is an ornithischian or an ankylosaurian, as its teeth resemble those of ankylosaurians like Sarcolestes and Gastonia.
Species based solely on teeth are generally not well accepted in paleontological consensus because dinosaur teeth are not distinctive enough to define a genus.
It has been proposed to move G. wucaiwanensis to a different genus, with "Eugongbusaurus" suggested as an informal replacement name.
